title: Introduce throttle-curve prefill optimizer and quantization safety certifier
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Tenant cold-start and bursty traffic patterns produce sharp cost spikes and wasted prefill work. This change introduces a throttle-curve based prefill optimizer that smooths tenant warmup across a configurable ramp (slope) and attaches a lightweight quantization safety certifier that simulates nominal unit-econ regressions before applying aggressive quant profiles. Goals: (1) reduce cold-start cost spikes by smoothing prefill ramp and avoiding burst-prefill over-provisioning; (2) provide a certifier that flags quant profiles likely to regress quality beyond an operator-set tolerance; (3) wire sane defaults into Console and CLI so first-time tenants get safe prefill/quant settings. Key ideas: - Throttle-curve: per-tenant ramp defined as a 3-point curve (initial fraction, slope, cap) that the autoscaler/prefill agent respects when scheduling warmup batches. The policy reduces parallel prefill concurrency during first N minutes to limit instantaneous token spend. - Optimizer: runs lightweight tenant trace replays to pick a ramp that meets a target cost uplift threshold while still meeting warm-start latency targets. - Quant certifier: runs a compact set of prompts through a proposed quant profile under both cached and cold paths; computes a regression score and blocks or tags the profile if above the tolerance. Implementation notes: single feature flag (prefill.throttle_curve.enabled) enabled by default for new tenants; optimizer is opt-in (CLI/Console) while certifier runs automatically on quant profile rollout. Backwards compatibility: existing prefill behavior preserved when flag is off. Rollout: staged canary (10 tenants), telemetry-backed watchdog, and automatic rollback on >5% unit-econ delta regression. Checklist: - [x] Core throttle curve runtime (Go) and policy engine - [x] Trace-based optimizer harness + synthetic replay CLI - [x] Quant certifier harness + small prompt-suite (50 items) - [x] Console defaults UI and API wiring - [x] Metrics and dashboards (prefill.slope, prefill.cost_delta, quant.cert_status) - [x] Integration tests and smoke test on canary fleet - [x] Docs: Console help text and runbook - [x] Linear tickets referenced for rollout and product sign-off Related: ENG-2375 (prefill ramping), ENG-2410 (quant certification), PM-428 (tenant onboarding economics).

review_thread: Diego Alvarez (reviewer): Nice work on the runtime. Two asks: limit the default slope to 0.2 for new tenants and add a guard so optimizer never recommends slope < 0.05.
Maya Chen (author): Done — set default_slope=0.2 and optimizer lower bound enforced in replay_sampler.go. Added unit tests covering the bound.

Rina Patel (reviewer): Quant certifier looks promising. Please ensure the prompt-suite includes churned examples (emoji, code, structured JSON). Also add a CI job that runs a fast smoke of 10 prompts to avoid regressions in CI timeouts.
Maya Chen (author): Expanded prompt-suite with 12 additional churned examples and added ci/quant-cert-smoke job. Reduced runtime of smoke to ~40s by sampling a subset when CI flag is set.
Omar Qureshi (approver): Verified canary telemetry on staging fleet. Approving for merge once green CI. One operational note: add a Grafana alert for prefill.cost_delta > 3% sustained 30m.
Maya Chen (author): Added grafana alert in telemetry/dashboard.json and documented response play in runbook. Thanks!
merge_outcome: Merged via squash by Rina Patel. Squash commit: 7a9c3d8, merge method: squash. Canary rollout started via scripts/canary-rollout.sh and monitored by telemetry team. No post-merge hotfixes required during staged rollout.
release_notes: Add throttle-curve prefill optimizer: smooths tenant warmup to reduce cold-start cost spikes; add quantization safety certifier to block high-regression quant profiles; Console defaults and CLI opt-ins included; metrics and alerts added for prefill cost delta.
